html: The Calvas were a people of the highlands of southern Loja, in Ecuador, near the border with Peru, around today's Cariamanga. They were one of several small groups of the region, with the Paltas, and are known only from Spanish reports. The Inca conquered the area in the late 1400s, on their road north to Quito. Under Spanish rule the Calvas were absorbed into the mixed population, and the canton of Calvas in Ecuador keeps their name. See also Garrochambas.
